note: AS-BUILT (0.29.0). Slice A derives plan readiness at read time (contract.PlanSections -> planWritten -> Feature.PlanUnwritten -> Feature.Authoring(), with PlanUnwrittenReason as the single reason clause every refusal quotes) and feeds the dim authoring pill, the gate counts, both accept paths, the footer chip and the drill note; the refusals sit OUTSIDE attemptActionForce's !force guards so the M force key cannot conjure an acceptance for a plan that does not exist. Slice B moves each phase's status write from exit to ENTRY (the phase skills) and makes the concurrency cap key on a live gogo-go BUILD session via the new launch.SessionAction / HasSessionAction parser, dropping cap.go's Class filter - the classification half of the under-count that let a second build clobber one working tree. Neither slice adds a status enum value: the frozen status enum, the four work-index classes and the class->column mapping are unchanged. No class diagram: the change adds one Feature field plus pure helpers on existing types, so a structure diagram would carry no signal the flow does not already carry. Fix round 01 added: the cap's user-visible rule is now a single shared constant (orchestrator.CapRuleClause) quoted by all four surfaces that state it, because three of the four hand-written copies had gone stale; FR8's refusal now also covers the reload AUTO-PICKUP path, the one launch path with no human in the loop; the render path decides through a pure planUnready(f) predicate instead of opening plan.md every frame; and tui.phaseLineLags derives a '· state lags' cue from the telemetry, so a phase skill that skips its occupancy write is VISIBLE rather than silent - which it was, on FR11's very first live run. Fix round 02 added: both cap refusals (board + headless) now name the TARGETED `gogo sweep <slug>` through the shared CapSweepRemedy, never the host-global bare form that reaps other sources' live builds as orphans; phaseLineLags gained a second arm so an ENTRY event naming a different phase than the line does is caught too (the loop back to implement, the pipeline's most common re-entry) plus a working-status whitelist so a terminal item with a lingering session never reads as lagging; and the cue arms are now provably mutually exclusive, which replaced an unpinned 'order matters' claim. Fix round 03 added: both config-tab cap WIRINGS are pinned (a rendered viewConfigRight assertion plus structural call-site checks on both producers, after the reviewer's D4/D5 probes showed the producers could stay correct while the surfaces went stale); CapRefusal makes CapSweepRemedy's empty-return contract real at both refusal sites; and the detector's documented reading was corrected - `. state lags` means state.md and events.jsonl disagree about the current phase (one half of step 1 did not land), and its silence is not proof of health, since a later mid-phase event can mask the phase-done arm. Phase-4 fix round (TEST-001, user's fix-now call): parseStateFile is block-comment aware - contract.advanceComment carries the open-`<!--` state across lines and any line starting inside a block is skipped - so the shipped template's commented-out `- **correlation:**` EXAMPLE no longer parses as a real field and no longer paints a bogus chain-x3 chip on a fresh scaffold. Same legend-leak family as FR6's stripPlaceholder, three lines away in the same function; single-line comment behaviour byte-for-byte unchanged, and every edge case (unterminated opener, stray closer, same-line pair, a key line that opens a block) decided toward 'missing, never wrong'. Phase-5 fix round (user's call): FR11's removal of the phases' EXIT write was an unintended consequence, not a design choice - with only the entry write (prose, skipped on all 3 live runs) state.md stopped advancing at all, which is worse than the one-phase lag this release set out to fix. The exit write is restored in all three phase skills alongside the entry write, and each says the redundancy IS the design. Consequence checked and pinned: arm A of the state-lags detector now also matches the brief healthy hand-off gap between one phase's exit write and the next phase's entry write (self-clearing, like the `building` chip), while the same shape stays lit for a whole phase when the entry write is genuinely skipped. Test round 3 (user's fix-now call): TEST-002 - the board's m/M never consulted Feature.WaitingForUser(), so a card paused at a DECISION GATE opened a real /gogo:go confirmation and only a STOP instruction inside the spawned session's own prompt stood between a keypress and a relaunch. That is prose enforcement, which this release's own evidence disproves, so the check now sits in attemptActionForce OUTSIDE every !force guard - the same shape as FR4a - and names the open decision's ID plus /gogo:resume. It pairs with REV-022's scoped exit write: a card that enters the gate stays there, keeps its gate signals, and is refused by both m and M, while a legitimate resume makes it launchable again (a gate you cannot leave would be worse than one you can bypass).

diagrams.title: As-built control flow: PlanSections/planWritten -> PlanUnwritten -> Authoring() drives the pill, the gate counts, the m/M bounce, the pure planUnready render predicate, the drill note, both accept gates and the unattended auto-pickup guard; SessionAction/HasSessionAction plus events.jsonl drive the cap, its single-sourced rule and targeted sweep remedy, the building/state-lags/stalled cues and the gogo status LIVE column

As-built build timing: gogo-implement writes phase=implement/status=implementing at ENTRY (1b), and a second m in the same source is refused because the cap counts the live gogo-go session even while the file still reads plan-accepted
As-built work-item lifecycle: the derived authoring state before acceptance, the entry-write transitions after it, and the derived stalled cue when a phase's session dies
